about: Hand-curated timeline events. 'chokepoints' lists the keys from transits.json an event bears on (empty for global, price-led events). 'kind' is one of conflict, accident, climate, policy, market, data. Figures quoted in a summary come from data/transits.json and data/prices.json unless the summary names another source.

events.title: Two tankers attacked in the Gulf of Oman
events.summary: Explosions damaged the tankers Front Altair and Kokuka Courageous just outside the strait. Washington blamed Iran, which denied involvement. Traffic through Hormuz did not fall.

events.title: Iran seizes the tanker Stena Impero
events.summary: Revolutionary Guards boarded the British-flagged tanker in the strait, and Britain told its ships to stay away for a time. Daily transits barely moved.

events.title: A week of faulty counts
events.summary: From 26 January to 2 February 2020 PortWatch's counts jump at five of the six chokepoints at once, to three or four times normal at Panama and the Cape. Panama cannot physically pass that many ships, so this is a fault in the source data, not a surge in traffic.

events.title: WHO calls COVID-19 a pandemic
events.summary: Lockdowns crushed oil demand and Brent fell from $36 a barrel to $9 by 21 April. Ship counts at these chokepoints held up far better than prices did.

events.title: Ever Given blocks the Suez Canal
events.summary: The 400-metre container ship ran aground and shut the canal for six days while more than 350 ships queued. PortWatch shows two transits on 25 March against a normal 50 to 60.

events.title: Counting change at Malacca
events.summary: PortWatch's Malacca count jumps by more than a third in a single week, across every ship type, with no matching move at any other chokepoint. This looks like a change in how transits are counted, not a surge in trade, so earlier Malacca figures are on a different basis.

events.title: Russia invades Ukraine
events.summary: Brent crossed $100 a barrel within days, for the first time since 2014, and peaked at $133 on 8 March. For these chokepoints it was a price shock, not a traffic one.

events.title: Drought forces Panama to cap transits
events.summary: With Gatun Lake low, the canal authority limited traffic to 32 ships a day, down from about 36 in normal conditions.

events.title: Panama cuts deeper
events.summary: After the driest October since 1950, booking slots dropped to 25 a day, then 24 and 22, with 18 planned for February. PortWatch counts bottomed at 18 to 21 a day in January 2024.

events.title: Houthis seize the Galaxy Leader
events.summary: Yemen's Houthis hijacked the car carrier in the Red Sea and took its 25 crew hostage, opening a campaign against merchant ships that they tied to the war in Gaza.

source.name: Associated Press via Anchorage Daily News

events.title: Container lines leave the Red Sea
events.summary: Maersk and Hapag-Lloyd paused sailings through Bab el-Mandeb after attacks on their ships, and MSC and CMA CGM followed a day later. Within two months Suez transits fell from about 75 a day to about 40, while traffic round the Cape rose from about 50 to about 90.

events.title: US and UK strike Houthi targets
events.summary: The first of many rounds of strikes in Yemen aimed to stop the attacks on shipping. Traffic did not come back.

events.title: Panama eases as rain returns
events.summary: Better rain in November let the canal authority drop its planned cut to 18 ships a day and lift daily slots to 24 instead.

events.title: Panama back to 36 slots a day
events.summary: The maximum draft returned to the full 50 feet on 15 August and booking slots to 36 on 1 September, ending a year of drought restrictions.

events.title: Trump vows to take back the canal
events.summary: In his inaugural address the US president claimed China was running the canal and said the United States was "taking it back". Panama's president rejected the claim. Traffic was unaffected.

events.title: Iran's parliament backs closing Hormuz
events.summary: After US strikes on Iranian nuclear sites, lawmakers endorsed closing the strait and left the decision to the security council. It stayed open: about 100 ships a day kept crossing, and Brent peaked near $80.

events.title: Two cargo ships attacked in the Red Sea
events.summary: Houthis attacked the bulk carrier Magic Seas on 6 July, forcing its crew to abandon ship, and hit the Eternity C a day later, killing three seafarers.

events.title: Houthis announce an end to shipping attacks
events.summary: A letter from the group's chief of staff said its campaign against Israel-linked shipping was over. Carriers did not rush back: three months later Suez transits were still about 40 a day, against about 75 before the crisis.

events.title: US and Israel strike Iran; Hormuz closes
events.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards warned ships off within hours, and the closure was confirmed on 2 March. PortWatch transits fell from roughly 100 a day in the last week of February to 3 a day in the first week of March, and Brent rose from $71 to a peak of $138 on 7 April.

events.title: US blockades Iranian ports
events.summary: A ceasefire on 8 April was meant to reopen the strait, but talks in Islamabad failed and the US Navy began stopping ships bound to or from Iran. Transits stayed mostly under 10 a day.

source.name: Wikipedia: 2026 United States naval blockade of Iran

events.title: US–Iran memorandum partly reopens Hormuz
events.summary: Crossings resumed the next day and the US lifted its blockade. PortWatch counted 513 ships from 18 June to 5 July, about 28 a day against roughly 100 before the war. Brent fell back to $69.

events.title: Truce collapses and the blockade returns
events.summary: Iran struck three ships on 6 and 7 July, the US answered with air strikes and reinstated its blockade on 14 July. Transits dropped back to about five a day.

events.title: Houthis declare a blockade on Saudi Arabia
events.summary: The group announced a blockade aimed at Bab el-Mandeb. Ship-tracking data showed crossings down about a quarter within nine days, from 42.5 a day to 32.1.

events.title: MSC ships return to the Red Sea
events.summary: The largest container line resumed transits with its own ships, making at least seven Bab el-Mandeb passages in two weeks without a formal announcement.

events.title: El Niño brings Panama's caps back
events.summary: Low rainfall led the canal authority to cut booking slots to 34 a day on 3 September and 32 on 15 September. On 28 September it eased to 33 from mid-October as rain improved.

events.title: Iran offers a seven-day plan to reopen Hormuz
events.summary: Tehran proposed reopening the strait a week after fighting stops, the US blockade lifts and sanctions ease, with nuclear talks to follow. No deal has followed.
